route: Work Permit (Entertainment: Arts, Culture and Sports category)

permit.applies: The employer, promoter, agent or producer (the sponsoring organisation), for each foreign artist or entertainer and each event, to the Ministry of Labour; the permit is shown to Immigration on arrival.
permit.first: Evidence of the engagement and the authorisation of the relevant Grenadian professional association or cultural organisation such as the Spicemas Corporation (its licence for any Carnival event); the sponsor shows it considered available Grenadian entertainers.

fees.what: Work permit, other Commonwealth citizens, North America, United Kingdom and EU nationals, per year of employment (SRO 26/2008)
Work permit, other foreign nationals, per year of employment (SRO 26/2008)

Work permit, individual entertainer from The Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Guyana, Jamaica, Montserrat, Suriname, Trinidad and Tobago or Cuba (SRO 26/2015; waived for CARICOM artistes by Cabinet directive of 15 May 2017)
Work permit, band from the same states (SRO 26/2015)

permit.union: The authorisation of the relevant Grenadian professional association or cultural organisation (such as the Spicemas Corporation); the Ministry processes the application if it doesn't object.
permit.eligibility: The applicant has an international reputation and record of excellence in their declared field, or ethnic significance, or is manifestly essential to the presentation or production (where necessary).

sources.title: Ministry of Labour, Work Permit Guidelines: A General Guide to the Foreign Nationals and Commonwealth Citizens Employment System in Grenada (June 2020)
sources.said: Employers, promoters, agents or producers are required to apply for Work Permits, for each foreign artist/entertainer, for all events. … Obtain the authorisation of the relevant Grenadian Professional Association or Cultural foundations/organizations such as Spicemas Corporation. … If the relevant Cultural Foundation/Spicemas Corporation or professional association does not object to the application, the Ministry of Labour will process the application, within the prescribed provisions. … The applicant has an international reputation and record of excellence in their declared field, or ethnic significance, or is manifestly essential to the presentation or production; … They have considered engaging available Grenadian entertainers or professionals; … that all new Work Permit applications and all renewal applications be processed, within 12 working days, providing all supporting documentations are in order. … Applications Forms: Non-refundable fee of one hundred Eastern Caribbean Dollars ($100.00 XCD), {SRO 48/2014}. … Other Commonwealth Citizens, North America, United Kingdom and European Union Nationals: Three Thousand Eastern Caribbean Dollars ($3,000.00 XCD), for each desired year of employment {SRO 26/2008}. … Foreign Nationals (other than those mentioned in #3): Five Thousand Eastern Caribbean Dollars ($5,000.00 XCD), for each desired year of employment {SRO 26/2008}. … CARICOM Entertainers: Waiver of Work Permit fees to CARICOM Artistes only (Cabinet Directive 15th May, 2017); … Work Permits are granted for a period of one year;

sources.title: S.R.O. 26 of 2015, Foreign Nationals and Commonwealth Citizens (Employment) (Amendment) Regulations 2015 (gazetted 17 July 2015)
sources.said: two thousand five hundred dollars, in respect of a band; … five hundred dollars, in respect of an individual entertainer.
